html:
The Balfour Declaration was a letter of 2 November 1917 in which Britain's foreign secretary, Arthur Balfour, backed a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine. Palestine was then part of the Ottoman Empire.

It added that nothing should be done to harm the civil and religious rights of the non-Jewish communities, who were then about nine in ten of the people. Britain hoped to win Jewish support in the First World War and to secure the land near the Suez Canal.

British troops took Jerusalem weeks later. The declaration was written into the British mandate over Palestine (Mandatory Palestine) in 1922, which opened the way for Jewish immigration under Zionism. Palestinians see it as the root of their loss.
sum: The Balfour Declaration was a letter of 2 November 1917 in which Britain's foreign secretary, Arthur Balfour, backed a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine. Palestine was then part of the Ottoman Empire.
